[User #1497315400 postsbananas_ozWhirlpool Forums Addict] I'm interested in what a large business absorbs in cash handling costs as opposed to cards. When I worked at an independent servo, the manager told us cards cost less and on occasion ran promos to encourage cash out on EFTPOS to minimise cash on hand even further.
[User #2920838253 poststomscoI did not get my spaghetti-o'sWhirlpool Forums Addict] Agree. We used to charge a CC surcharge, I pushed so hard to get rid of it.
Lost/stolen cash and the man hours going to bank to deposit are a huge cost.
[User #1208174477 postsHaklinWhirlpool Forums Addict] PAYMENT HANDLING FEE (ONLINE) -$0.95
So annoyed by this bPay fee. Don't use this card aside from international transactions or when overseas and this is just a rort. Guess I'll end up using the fee free feature through the site, annoying!
[User #73789824 postsHearthStone25I'm new here, please be nice] I only ever used this card for oversea purchase and I pay out the lot when the bill is due and wonder what that 95c is for, now I know
[User #669436181 postsLeginagThere is no chicken...Whirlpool Forums Addict] Anyone else had issues with mail from 28D? My card was cancelled due to suspected fraud. 3 weeks later (5-10 business days is their timeframe) nothing, so I ring them and they say they will send a new one out with priority. The next day the original replacement arrives – but they'd already cancelled it. I'm at 3 weeks waiting for the second card to arrive. Going to wait it out before reporting it. I suspect part of it is AusPost being slow – but has anyone else experienced this?
[User #444901028 postsIpswich ResidentNBN is here!Whirlpool Enthusiast] Just got hit with the fee. I don't think the wording on the previous statement was entirely clear. Guess I should have called them to clarify. Might be time to close my account.
[User #791022770 postsThe ZiggsterzZZzSection Moderator] Queanbeyan writes...
I don't think the wording on the previous statement was entirely clear
What wasnt clear about a 95c fee if you pay by BPay??
[User #3783017498 postsSir Tony OAMI am not a robotWhirlpool Forums Addict] The Ziggster writes...
What wasnt clear about a 95c fee if you pay by BPay??
I think we are ALL CLEAR with this stupid 'fee / charge' – however what is SO STUPID about is this :
Amount must be less than or equal to your Current Balance
There is no ability to ADD any $ amount you wish – eg – to push the account into 'credit' prior to going away using this function.
Sure...... it's only 95c..... the point is that they have introduced 'functionality' that is pointless. I'm sure that I'm not alone in using this card in 'credit' mode for trips.
[User #101021729 postsMr GimletWerewolves, not swearwolvesSection Moderator] Sir Tony OAM writes...
'm sure that I'm not alone in using this card in 'credit' mode for trips
I think you're probably in a small minority though. I certainly want the interest free period; if I wanted to have a positive balance I'd be using my Citibank Plus since it's more useful for ATMs as well as purchases.
[User #2920838253 poststomscoI did not get my spaghetti-o'sWhirlpool Forums Addict] Sir Tony OAM writes...
Amount must be less than or equal to your Current Balance
If you read their T&C's, cardholders are not liable for any loss through negligence in excess of their credit limit.
If I recall correctly, this will apply for all credit cards. This puts them at unnecessary risk, so they choose to discourage it.
As Mr Gimlet said, if you want excess funds, you can use a Citibank Plus card with however much you want on it.
[User #372952858 postsGBNWhirlpool Enthusiast] Hi, just wondering if I can reduce my credit limit for 28 degrees card.
I applied many years ago and my cc limit is at $4500 but I have applied other card so I only need this card for free overseas transaction online purchases (which I don't do much these days)
Will I be able to reduced my limit to like 1k? or is that not possible anymore?
From what I see ,currently there is min limit of $6000 if you want this card ATM
[User #401174107 postsDRP535In the penalty box] Sir Tony OAM writes...
I'm sure that I'm not alone in using this card in 'credit' mode for trips.
What makes you so "sure" about that? I very much doubt that many people choose to use a credit card as a quasi-debit card. Why would you when there's a perfectly good and free debit card that does that exact task better and cheaper available from Citibank?
There used to be a valid argument for putting the 28D card into positive balance. Back before the card was upgraded to Platinum status, GE were being very stingey with credit limits and putting the account into positive balance as a temporary and rather crude way to increase the amount you could spend with it was a valid thing to do. I even did so myself once when I first got the card and had only a $1,000 limit, I needed to purchase something worth twice that much from the UK with it. I was actually advised to put the card into credit by the GE CSR I rang to inquire about a credit limit increase.
But today, now that the card is Platinum with the requisite $6,000 min credit limit, there is no such argument anymore for putting it into credit balance.
[User #401174107 postsDRP535In the penalty box] LUFEE84 writes...
Will I be able to reduced my limit to like 1k? or is that not possible anymore?
Probably not, but give them a call and tell us what happens. If your card has already been upgraded to the Platinum version, then I'd say your chance of a limit decrease are slim. The stated min limit is 6K and you're already under that as a virtue of being a legacy cardholder from the non-Platinum days. If however you still have a valid non-Platinum card that hasn't been upgraded yet due to natural expiration, then you might have a better argument and a slightly better chance of lowering the limit I guess. Ask them and see, and then tell us what they said.
[User #297689924 postsdennis_3107Whirlpool Enthusiast] DRP535 writes...
What makes you so "sure" about that? I very much doubt that many people choose to use a credit card as a quasi-debit card. Why would you when there's a perfectly good and free debit card that does that exact task better and cheaper available from Citibank?
You dont have to use it as a quasi-debit card.
What's wrong with using it just as a credit card. More secure anyway. I have both cards, and only withdraw cash from my Citi card if it is absolutely needed. Otherwise, credit card for the win, to shelter myself from any fraud or stolen money.
[User #3783017498 postsSir Tony OAMI am not a robotWhirlpool Forums Addict] tomsco writes...
if you want excess funds, you can use a Citibank Plus card with however much you want on it.
I have both the 28D and CitiPlus.... just 'noted' that I have over $700 on it – I barely ever use this card.(last used in Feb) .. might have to revert back to it rather than 28D.
